ai.description: This slender snake reaches 50–90 cm. It is olive-brown with two distinct, longitudinal yellow or cream lateral stripes and dark crossbars. Key features include prominent keeled scales and white lips.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue for *Amphiesma stolatum* is the pair of prominent, pale yellow or cream-colored longitudinal stripes running along the back of its olive-brown body.
ai.habitat: The Buff Striped Keelback inhabits moist grasslands, paddy fields, and marshy areas across the Indian subcontinent, typically ranging from lowlands up to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: When threatened, the Buff Striped Keelback often flattens its neck to appear larger and may freeze or flee into nearby water to escape potential predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Amphiesma stolatum* is oviparous, typically breeding during the monsoon (June–August). Females lay clutches of 5–15 eggs in underground burrows or decaying vegetation.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Buff Striped Keelback is widespread across the Indian subcontinent, occurring from the plains up to 2,000m elevation in diverse habitats across most Indian states.
